Measured phase compositions (EPMA, wt.%): γ austenite Mn 35.92, Al 5.88, C 0.098, Nb 0.09, V 0.09, Mo 1.12, W 0.86; α ferrite Mn 32.44, Al 6.83, C not reported, Nb 0.09, V 0.18, Mo 1.54, W 1.63 (Table 1, b0017).
Reduction of area: 78 ± 0.5 % at RT and 80 ± 1 % at LNT (Table 2).
True stress values (Table 3): RT 339, 483, 635, 723, 800 MPa at 3, 10, 20, 28, 38 % engineering strain (55 % not measured); LNT 598, 778, 1007, 1148, 1280, 1463 MPa at 3, 10, 20, 28, 38, 55 %.
Corresponding true strains: 3.0, 9.5, 18.2, 24.7, 32.2, 43.8 % at engineering strains 3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0, 38.0, 55.0 % (Table 3).
Geometrically necessary dislocation density ρ^GND (EBSD-α, 10^14 m^-2): RT 0.71, 3.05, 5.64, 7.92, 8.99; LNT 0.97, 2.59, 5.95, 6.93, 9.17, 9.73 (Table 3).

Cell/dislocation-cell block (CBs or DCs) sizes: RT 448 ± 74 nm at 20 % and 282 ± 56 nm at 28 %; LNT 429 ± 76 nm at 20 % and 242 ± 54 nm at 28 % (Table 3); CBs/DCs refined more at LNT than RT at equivalent strain.

Lattice friction stresses: 143 MPa for RT deformation and 389 MPa for LNT deformation; initial grain-boundary strengthening about 108 MPa; twin strengthening contribution 290 MPa at 55 % LNT strain; ferrite dislocation strengthening < 10 MPa (neglected).
Strengthening contributions σ_dis(γ) (MPa): RT 48, 207, 347, 434, 474 at 3–38 %; LNT 58, 240, 379, 469, 504, 646 at 3–55 %. σ_dis(α) (GND): RT 1, 4, 6, 8, 8; LNT 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 (Table 6).
The process notes flag an inconsistency: the quench is described as 'oil quenching' (b0015) but the tensile specimens are described as cut from 'water quenched steel samples' (b0026).

Taylor factor M distribution along TA: corner values 001 = 2.30, 111 = 3.64, 101 = 3.64; dashed boundary separates M < 2.7 and M > 3.06 regions; 'Twins' regions correspond to high-Taylor-factor orientations (type II and III grains) (Fig. 12).

Schmid factor evolution: RT {111}<110>γ peaks near 3 % strain then declines; RT {111}<112>γ stays higher than {111}<110> throughout; both LNT Schmid factors ({111}<110> and {111}<112>) peak at ~10 % engineering strain (Fig. 4).

Hall–Petch constant K estimated as 0.350 MPa·m^0.5 by linear fitting of yield strengths 267, 258, 251, 245 MPa against D^-0.5 for average grain sizes 8.2, 9.3, 10.8, 12.1 μm at solution temperatures 1000, 1025, 1050, 1075 °C, respectively; K is close to TWIP steels (0.357 and 0.330 MPa·m^0.5).
The grain-type classification (Gutierrez-Urrutia): type I = <001>//TA with ~15° deviation; type III = <111>//TA with ~15° deviation; type II = remaining orientations.
Deformation twinning onset: ~28 % tensile strain at RT vs ~10 % tensile strain at LNT, indicating strong dependence on deformation strain and temperature.
No κ-carbides present in the low-carbon low-density steel (beneficial to toughness); retained ferrite ~3 % refines austenite grains and enhances impact toughness.
XRD austenite volume fractions after LNT tensile deformation: 95.6 % (0 %), 97.3 % (3 %), 95.7 % (10 %), 96.8 % (28 %), 96.1 % (55 %), showing essentially stable austenite with a small BCC fraction.

The intercritical/SFT calculation evaluates γ_SFE (62.64/49.46 mJ·m^-2) exceeding the 20–45 mJ·m^-2 range typical for twinning, so SFE is not the sole decisive factor controlling twinning in this steel.
